AI industry leaders. The White House has been featuring a countdown clock leading up to the

The U.S. Supreme Court opens its new term next week. Justice Samuel Alito will not participate
in the high court's first case to be argued. It's a major test of if and when state and local
governments can sue fossil fuel companies. NPR's Nina Totenberg reports this is over allegations
the companies allegedly deceived the public about environmental harms that companies knew existed.
Alito has long held financial interest in energy companies but did not recuse himself last February
when the Supreme Court agreed to hear a major climate change case. Now, however, one week
before arguments in the case are to take place, the court indicated that Alito will not participate.
While he gave no reason, it appears that he owns stock in two companies facing similar lawsuits
that have been paused while the Supreme Court ponders the issue. Alito's decision could lead
to a four-to-four tie at the high court, but most climate change experts see that as unlikely given
that the case is viewed as a long shot. Nina Totenberg, NPR News, Washington. You're listening
to NPR. The Trump administration banned about one billion dollars in Canadian products overnight.
These include alcohol and dairy. This is part of President Trump's trade war against Canada.
NASA and Boeing are once again moving forward with a plan to launch astronauts to the international
space station using Boeing's spacecraft, the Starliner. This comes after the last crew to fly

From central Florida public media, Brendan Byrne has more. In February, NASA released a report that
